title: What Does "Caliber" Mean and Why is it Important?
summary: Learn the difference between .61 and .68 caliber Byrna launchers, why caliber matters, and how to choose the correct projectiles for reliable performance and effective less-lethal self-defense.
body_text: What Does Caliber Mean? Understanding .61 Caliber vs .68 Caliber Byrna Launchers If you've been shopping for a Byrna launcher , you've probably noticed two different caliber options: .61 caliber and .68 caliber. It's one of the most common questions from new Byrna owners, and while the terminology may sound technical, the answer is actually straightforward. Understanding caliber will help ensure you purchase the correct launcher, compatible projectiles, and the setup that best fits your personal defense needs. What Is Caliber? Caliber simply refers to the diameter of the projectile fired by the launcher. In the Byrna lineup, there are two sizes: .61 caliber projectiles .68 caliber projectiles The most important thing to remember is that these projectiles are not interchangeable . If you own a Byrna CL or Byrna CL-XL , you'll need .61 caliber projectiles . If you own a Byrna SD or Byrna LE , you'll need .68 caliber projectiles . Using the wrong caliber is like putting the wrong size battery into a device—it simply won't work correctly. Does a Smaller Caliber Mean Less Power? A common misconception is that the smaller .61 caliber projectile is less capable than a .68 caliber round. In reality, caliber alone doesn't determine performance. The Byrna CL platform is engineered to launch its .61 caliber projectiles at speeds of over 400 feet per second , while many .68 caliber launchers operate closer to 300 feet per second . Each launcher is specifically designed around its own projectile size to deliver reliable performance. Rather than comparing caliber by size alone, it's better to choose the launcher that best matches your intended use and carrying preferences. Choosing the Right Byrna Setup Whether selecting a compact everyday carry option like the Byrna CL or a full-size launcher like the Byrna LE or Byrna SD , always purchase projectiles that match the caliber of your launcher. If you're still unsure which Byrna launcher is right for your needs, taking Byrna's product recommendation quiz is an excellent place to start. Understanding caliber makes shopping easier, helps avoid purchasing incompatible ammunition, and ensures your Byrna launcher is always ready with the correct projectiles when you need them most.

body_text: BEDFORD, Mass.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jul. 27, 2026-- Stoke Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: STOK) is a biotechnology company dedicated to restoring protein expression by harnessing the body’s potential with RNA medicine and has a lead investigational medicine, zorevunersen, in development as a first-in-class potential disease-modifying treatment for Dravet syndrome. Today, the Company announced that management will host a webcast and conference call for analysts and investors on Monday, August 3, 2026, at 4:30 p.m. ET, to discuss second quarter 2026 business and financial updates. The webcast will be available on the Investors & News section of Stoke’s website at https://investor.stoketherapeutics.com/ . Research analysts who plan to join the call and participate in the Q&A session may register here to receive the dial-in details and a unique PIN. All other participants are invited to access the listen-only webcast by clicking here . An archived replay of the webcast will be available for at least 90 days following the event. About Stoke Therapeutics Stoke Therapeutics (Nasdaq: STOK), is a biotechnology company dedicated to restoring protein expression by harnessing the body’s potential with RNA medicine. Using Stoke’s proprietary TANGO (Targeted Augmentation of Nuclear Gene Output) approach, Stoke is developing antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) to selectively restore naturally-occurring protein levels. Stoke’s first medicine in development, zorevunersen, has demonstrated the potential for disease modification in patients with Dravet syndrome and is currently being evaluated in a Phase 3 study. Stoke’s initial focus are diseases of the central nervous system and the eye that are caused by a loss of ~50% of normal protein levels (haploinsufficiency). Proof of concept has been demonstrated in other organs, tissues, and systems, supporting broad potential for Stoke’s proprietary approach. Stoke is headquartered in Bedford, Massachusetts. For more information, visit https://www.stoketherapeutics.com/ and follow us on LinkedIn . About Zorevunersen Zorevunersen is an investigational antisense oligonucleotide that is designed to treat the underlying cause of Dravet syndrome by increasing functional NaV1.1 protein production in brain cells from the unaffected (wild-type) copy of the SCN1A gene. This highly differentiated mechanism of action aims to reduce seizure frequency beyond what has been achieved with anti-seizure medicines and to improve neurodevelopment, cognition and behavior. Zorevunersen has demonstrated the potential for disease modification and has been granted orphan drug designation by the FDA and the EMA. The FDA has also granted zorevunersen rare pediatric disease designation and Breakthrough Therapy Designation for the treatment of Dravet syndrome with a confirmed mutation not associated with gain-of-function in the SCN1A gene, and China’s Center for Drug Evaluation has granted zorevunersen Breakthrough Therapy Designation. Stoke has a strategic collaboration with Biogen (Nasdaq: BIIB) to develop and commercialize zorevunersen for Dravet syndrome. Under the collaboration, Stoke retains exclusive rights for zorevunersen in the United States, Canada, and Mexico; Biogen receives exclusive rest of world commercialization rights. Zorevunersen is currently in clinical development, and its safety and efficacy have not been evaluated by any regulatory authority. title: Cooking with Chris: Three Generations, One Bowl of Wontons
summary: Hilton President & CEO Chris Nassetta discovers how a simple bowl of wontons at Waldorf Astoria Shanghai Qiantan tells a story.
body_text: Listen to this article 0:00 Follow Hilton President & CEO Chris Nassetta as he discovers how a simple bowl of wontons at Waldorf Astoria Shanghai Qiantan tells a story of family, tradition and three generations of hospitality In the latest episode of “Cooking with Chris,” Hilton President & CEO Chris Nassetta joins Waldorf Astoria Shanghai Qiantan Director of Food & Beverage Mandela Zhu to prepare one of China's most beloved comfort foods. Discover why wontons have long symbolized home, connection and togetherness in Chinese culture, bringing generations together through the simple act of cooking and sharing a meal. Go behind the scenes to learn how family traditions, culinary heritage and a multi-generational love of hospitality come together around the kitchen table. The most beloved recipes carry with them memories, traditions and the comforting feeling of home. In the latest episode of “Cooking with Chris,” Hilton President & CEO Chris Nassetta travels to Waldorf Astoria Shanghai Qiantan , where one of China's most cherished dishes becomes the starting point for a conversation that reaches far beyond the kitchen. Alongside Director of Food & Beverage Mandela Zhu, Chris prepares wontons, sharing in a cooking ritual that’s steeped in traditions that celebrate togetherness one fold at a time. For generations, families across China have gathered around the table to prepare wontons together. The process is simple but meaningful, and in this video, Chris and Mandela talk about the important role food plays in uniting people. Mandela shares that his own mother never fully revealed her recipe to him as she wanted an excuse for them to keep cooking together and, for him, wontons are the perfect representation of love. He describes the delicate wrapper as a symbol of protection, wrapping the filling with the same care that families show when wrapping one another with support. Today, he continues this storied tradition with his own daughter, who has already developed a passion for culinary arts. Hospitality has become a family tradition, too. Mandela's father joined the original Shanghai Hilton in 1995, and as a young boy, Mandela regularly accompanied him to the hotel, where those early visits inspired his own career with Hilton. Now, his daughter dreams of becoming a chef and hopes to one day join Hilton herself, creating a remarkable three-generation legacy. Now, it’s your turn. Bring this meaningful taste of Shanghai into your own kitchen by following the full recipe below and discover how one simple dish can bring family and friends together, wherever home may be. Winter Wontons Recipe Ingredients 1.8 oz (about ⅓ cup packed, after squeezing dry) Chinese greens (qing cai) 1.8 oz (about ⅓ cup packed, after squeezing dry) Shepherd’s purse (ji cai) 1.8 oz (about ¼ cup minced) Pork back fat 3.9 oz (about ½ cup minced) Pork leg meat ¼ tsp Dark soy sauce 1 Tbsp Light soy sauce 1 Tbsp Oyster sauce 2 tsp Hot rendered pork lard 1 Large egg White pepper to taste Salt to taste Extras : 5 Wonton wrappers Soup Base : - ¾ cup + 1 Tbsp Pork stock - 1 tsp Light soy sauce - ½ tsp Sesame oil - Salt to taste - White pepper to taste - 1 tsp Lard Garnish : - 1 Tbsp Dried shrimp - ¼ cup Seaweed - 1 Tbsp Chopped spring onion - 2 Tbsp Slices egg omelette Directions Blanch green leafy vegetables in boiling water for 20 seconds, then transfer to ice water. Squeeze out all excess water and set aside. Mince pork back fat and pork leg meat with a meat grinder, grind twice for fine texture. Place all filling ingredients in a bowl, stir clockwise until fully combined. Heat lard and pour it over the filling, stirring clockwise until fully incorporated. Chill the prepared filling in the refrigerator for 6 hours before wrapping wontons. Place a portion of filling in the center of a wonton wrapper, fold the wrapper in half. Overlap the two opposite corners to form a gold ingot shape. Bring water to a rolling boil and add wontons. The recommended water-to-wonton ratio is 9:1 to preserve the tender texture of wrappers during cooking. After the water re-boils, pour in a small amount of cold water and wait for it to boil again. Repeat this process three times, then remove the wontons. Place cooked wontons in a bowl, add lard, light soy sauce, sesame oil, white pepper, salt and prepared stock. Finish with garnishes: sliced egg omelette, dried shrimp, chopped spring onion and seaweed. Summer Wontons with Peanut Sauce Recipe Ingredients 1.8 oz (about ⅓ cup packed, after squeezing dry) Chinese greens (qing cai) 1.8 oz (about ⅓ cup packed, after squeezing dry) Shepherd’s purse (ji cai） 1.8 oz (about ¼ cup minced) Pork back fat 3.9 oz (about ½ cup minced) Pork leg meat ¼ tsp Dark soy sauce 1 Tbsp Light soy sauce 1 Tbsp Oyster sauce 2 tsp Hot rendered pork lard 1 Whole egg White pepper to taste Salt to taste Extras : 5 Wonton wrappers Dressing : - 3 Tbsp Sesame Paste - 2 tsp Light soy sauce - 2 tsp Vinegar - 1 tsp Oyster sauce - 1 tsp Sugar - 6 Tbsp + 2 tsp (about ⅓ cup + 1 tsp) Still water Garnish: - 1 Tbsp Chopped spring onion - Chili oil to taste Directions Blanch green leafy vegetables in boiling water for 20 seconds, then transfer to ice water. Squeeze out all excess water and set aside. Mince pork back fat and pork leg meat with a meat grinder, grind twice for fine texture. Place all filling ingredients in a bowl, stir clockwise until fully combined. Heat lard and pour it over the filling, stirring clockwise until fully incorporated. Chill the prepared filling in the refrigerator for 6 hours before wrapping wontons. Place a portion of filling in the center of a wonton wrapper, fold the wrapper in half. Overlap the two opposite corners to form a gold ingot shape. Bring water to a rolling boil and add wontons. The recommended water-to-wonton ratio is 9:1 to preserve the tender texture of wrappers during cooking. After the water re-boils, pour in a small amount of cold water and wait for it to boil again. Repeat this process three times, then remove the wontons. When making sesame paste, mineral water should be added slowly in a clockwise direction. After mixing evenly, add other ingredients and refrigerate for later use. Pour the sesame paste and chili oil over the wontons and sprinkle with chopped scallions. This episode takes place at Waldorf Astoria Shanghai Qiantan in Shanghai, China, where Chris Nassetta and Mandela Zhu prepare one of China’s most cherished dishes and explore how food, family and hospitality bring generations together. The episode highlights wontons, one of China’s most beloved comfort foods. title: The Best Summer Perfumes for Women in 2026: Fresh, Flirty Scents for the Heat
summary: The 12 best summer perfumes for women in 2026, split by moment: fresh daytime scents, flirty date-night picks, and beachy vacation gourmands. Find your warm-weather scent.
body_text: The best summer perfumes for women capture exactly how we want to feel when the heat hits: fresh, flirty, and unbothered. The amber-drenched, oud-heavy scents that felt so seductive in December? By July, they’re less “mysterious evening” and more “why is everyone backing away from me on the subway.” Heat doesn’t lie, and neither does your skin once the temperature climbs past 85. What Makes a Perfume Work in Summer Heat? What’s with the skin and warm weather? Summer’s high temperatures speed up how fast fragrance molecules evaporate off your skin, so your scents project harder and faster. A scent that reads as rich and layered at 65 degrees can turn heavy, even headache-inducing, at 95. That’s why deep orientals—thick ambers, dense incenses, that vanilla you loved all winter—tend to become overpowering once the heat sets in. Their whole appeal is slow, building intensity, and intensity is the last thing you want radiating off you at a rooftop happy hour or in a sweltering summer office. So what are the best summer perfumes? First up, let’s talk notes. Specifically, bright, fresh, uplifting top notes. Citrus, white florals, and watery greens (think bergamot, neroli, crisp cucumber, sheer jasmine) give a scent radiance and lift instead of density. In cooler months, a fragrance that fades in twenty minutes can feel like a letdown. In summer, that quick turnover is part of the appeal: a burst of freshness instead of a wall of scent following you into every room. Then there’s projection, which matters just as much as note choice. For summer, moderate’s the winner—scents that sit near to the skin rather than billowing outwards. Warmer air and more skin exposure already mean your fragrance is doing more work than usual; it doesn’t need to fight for attention three feet away, too. This is part of why skin scents feel so right in summer: soft musks, sheer woods, flirty scents that invite people to lean in and get closer. None of this means summer has to mean boring, and it definitely doesn’t mean one scent for every version of the season. The fragrance that gets you through a scorching afternoon errand run isn’t the one you want on a warm night out, and neither is quite right for salt air and sand. Below, we’ve broken twelve of the best summer scents for women into exactly those three moments—daytime, date night, and beach—so you know which bottle to reach for and when. Daytime Picks: Light Perfumes for Hot Weather When the sun is at full strength, you want your 2026 summer perfume to work with the heat instead of fighting it. These four picks lean on citrus, white florals, and watery greens—the notes that stay crisp when everything else wilts. Burberry — Brit Sheer The name says it all: Brit Sheer is summer citrus at its most transparent. Tangy yuzu and green pineapple leaf open the scent like a window thrown open on a bright morning, before soft peony and juicy lychee settle in for the day. It’s polished without being precious, the fragrance equivalent of a white linen shirt that never wrinkles. Wear it to the office, to brunch, to the farmers market; it works everywhere and never overstays its welcome. When to wear it: Weekday mornings when you need to feel put-together before your iced coffee kicks in. Deck of Scarlet — Siren Spell Jasmine can go heavy fast in the heat, but Deck of Scarlet’s Siren Spell keeps it coastal. Sparkling bergamot crashes in first like a cool wave, then salty neroli and jasmine weave together into a floral heart that feels sea-sprayed rather than hothouse. A base of cedar and sundrenched skin keeps everything grounded and close. It’s a white floral with an undertow—daytime-appropriate, but with an agenda. When to wear it: Long lunches that might turn into long afternoons. Marc Jacobs — Daisy Eau So Fresh Some fragrances just smell like a good mood, and Daisy Eau So Fresh is the reigning champion. Sparkling grapefruit and juicy raspberry open with pure effervescence, while pear, violet, and apple blossom keep the heart soft, dewy, and eau-so easy to wear. It’s the definition of a fresh perfume for summer: light enough for a heatwave, pretty enough that you’ll keep reaching for it well into September. When to wear it: Any day that involves sundresses, spontaneous plans, or both. Confessions of a Rebel — V-Edgy Green goes rogue in V-Edgy, where crisp cucumber skin and tart rhubarb meet bright yuzu and sheer jasmine for the coolest scent in the garden. This is the pick for anyone who finds most summer fragrances too sweet—it’s fresh with a bite, like cucumber water someone spiked with attitude. White musk in the base keeps it clean and skin-close, so it never crowds a hot day. When to wear it: Peak-heat afternoons when everything (and everyone) needs to chill. Warm-Night Picks: Summer Date Night Perfumes Summer evenings are their own season—golden light, bare shoulders, plans that start at eight and end whenever. These are the flirty, skin-close scents built for exactly that. Consider this your summer date night perfume shortlist. (And if you want to go deeper on this category, our guide to perfumes that attract men has you covered.) Love Island x Scentbird — Love Island The official scent of catching feelings on a warm night. Bombshell peach and bright yuzu open juicy and playful, then bare-skin musk takes over and keeps things very, very close. It smells like the moment right before something happens—sun-warmed, flirtatious, one hundred percent your type. If summer romance had a signature scent, this would be it. When to wear it: First dates, second dates, and any recoupling in between. Emily in Paris x Michel Germain — Romantic “Ah, romance! Exquisite romance!” Crisp green apple opens bright and hopeful, softening into pink peony and blooming magnolia—pure Parisian-summer-evening energy. Velvety blonde woods and a hint of musk in the base beckon with soft abandon, giving the scent just enough warmth for after dark without ever feeling heavy. It’s the fragrance version of an evening stroll along the Seine, even if your actual evening involves a patio and a spritz. When to wear it: Dinner dates where you want to be remembered as effortlessly charming. Confessions of a Rebel — Get a Room and Order Champagne The name is the instruction manual. Juicy raspberry and mandarin get the evening started with a fizzy, champagne-bright opening, before the scent settles into something darker and more seductive—the after-hours sibling of a sweet fruity floral. It’s playful on the surface and smoldering underneath, which is exactly the range you want from a summer night that has options. When to wear it: Nights when “one drink” was never really the plan. Burberry — My Burberry Blush For a softer kind of romance, My Burberry Blush is a rose that caught the last of the sunlight. Zesty lemon and crisp apple lift the opening, while pomegranate adds a jewel-toned juiciness to delicate rose petals and jasmine. It reads elegant rather than loud—a warm-evening floral that whispers instead of announcing. The kind of scent that makes someone ask what you’re wearing, quietly, so no one else hears the answer. When to wear it: Rooftop dinners, garden parties, and slow summer evenings that deserve a little polish. Beach & Vacation Picks: Salt, Coconut, and Solar Gourmands Vacation scents get to break the rules a little. Out here, gourmand sweetness works—as long as it comes with salt air, coconut, or that sun-on-skin glow the fragrance world calls “solar.” These four smell like the best week of your year. Juliette Has a Gun — Vanilla Vibes Proof that vanilla belongs at the beach. Fleur de sel—actual sea salt—opens the scent with a briny freshness that keeps the organic vanilla underneath from ever turning sugary. The result smells like skin after a day in the ocean: warm, salty, faintly sweet, completely addictive. It’s the rare vanilla that feels lighter the hotter it gets, which is why it’s become a warm-weather cult favorite. When to wear it: Beach days, boat days, and the tan-line season in general. Room 1015 — Wavechild A love letter to surf culture, Wavechild rides in on juicy orange and watermelon before creamy coconut and ambergris pull the whole thing into salty, sun-bleached territory. It’s nostalgic in the best way—boardwalks, surfboard wax, that one perfect beach summer—but built with niche-level craft. Bold enough to be memorable, breezy enough to wear in real heat. When to wear it: Vacation mode: activated. Bonus points if there’s an actual wave involved. Ariana Grande — Cloud Cloud earned its icon status for a reason: it’s a gourmand that floats. Airy lavender blossom and juicy pear lift the opening, while whipped coconut, praline, and vanilla orchid melt into a base that sits on the skin like—well, like a cloud. On a warm evening it turns softly solar, radiating that just-got-back-from-somewhere-sunny warmth. Sweet, but weightless about it. When to wear it: Sunset strolls, hotel-balcony evenings, and the flight home when you want to smell like the vacation lasted. Clean Reserve — Whipped Cherry Cherry, but make it tropical. Wild cherry gets a poolside makeover with juicy pineapple and coconut water up top, before almond blossom and mimosa soften the heart and a praline–vanilla cream base delivers dessert. It’s a fruity gourmand engineered for warm weather—sweet without the syrup, playful without the cloy, and crafted with Clean Reserve’s signature sustainably sourced ingredients. When to wear it: Pool parties, tropical getaways, and every frozen-drink occasion of the season. How to Try 12 Summer Scents (Without Buying 12 Bottles) Here’s the uncomfortable math of seasonal fragrance: a full bottle runs $80–$190, you’ll realistically wear it hard for three months a year, and you won’t know if it turns cloying on your skin at 95 degrees until you’ve already paid for it. Multiply that by a daytime scent, a date-night scent, and a vacation scent, and summer starts looking expensive. That’s exactly the problem a fragrance subscription solves. With Scentbird, you get a generous 8 ml travel spray of any scent in our 1,000+ fragrance catalog delivered monthly, roughly 120 sprays, enough to genuinely live with a fragrance through heatwaves, beach days, and warm nights before committing to a full bottle. Build a summer queue with a few picks from this list, swap in something new each month, and by September you’ll know which one earned permanent-collection status. Not sure where to start? Take our fragrance quiz and we’ll match you with summer scents based on your actual preferences, no guesswork required. The Quick Verdict: Our Top Pick Per Category Best daytime summer perfume: Marc Jacobs Daisy Eau So Fresh — the fresh, sparkling crowd-pleaser that makes hot days feel easy. Best summer date night perfume: Love Island x Scentbird Love Island — peach, yuzu, and bare-skin musk with maximum flirt factor. Best beach & vacation scent: Juliette Has a Gun Vanilla Vibes — salty-sweet perfection that smells better the hotter it gets. body_text: View All News Atmus Filtration Technologies Reports First Quarter 2026 Results May 1, 2026 NASHVILLE, Tenn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Atmus Filtration Technologies Inc. (Atmus; NYSE: ATMU), a global leader in filtration and media solutions, today reported financial results for its first quarter that ended March 31, 2026. First Quarter Highlights Net sales of $478 million Power Solutions segment net sales of $439 million Industrial Solutions segment net sales of $38 million GAAP net income of $48 million Diluted earnings per share of $0.59 Adjusted earnings per share of $0.69 Adjusted EBITDA of $95 million and Adjusted EBITDA margin of 19.8% Power Solutions Segment Adjusted EBITDA of $86 million and Adjusted EBITDA margin of 19.6% Industrial Solutions Segment Adjusted EBITDA of $8 million and Adjusted EBITDA margin of 21.9% Cash provided by operating activities was $38 million Adjusted free cash flow was $33 million Atmus completed the acquisition of Koch Filter Corporation (“Koch Filter”) on January 7, 2026. The portfolio addition established Atmus’ Industrial Solutions segment, where Koch Filter results are reported. With the acquisition, Atmus reports on two business segments: Power Solutions, which serves global on- and off-highway equipment markets through its Fleetguard® brand; and Industrial Solutions, which addresses commercial and industrial HVAC applications, and high-growth end markets including data centers and power generation environments through its Koch Filter® brand. 2026 Outlook The company is reaffirming guidance for the full year 2026 as follows: Total company Net sales to be in the range of $1,945 million to $2,015 million Power Solutions segment expected to be in the range of $1,790 million to $1,850 million Industrial Solutions segment expected to be in the range of $155 million to $165 million Adjusted EBITDA margin to be in the range of 19.5% to 20.5% Adjusted earnings per share in the range of $2.75 to $3.00 During the quarter, Atmus repurchased $7 million of common stock under the $150 million share repurchase program authorized by the Board of Directors in July 2024. As of March 31, 2026 , $62 million was remaining under the authorization. Additionally, Atmus paid a quarterly cash dividend of $0.055 per share of common stock. “The Atmus team delivered strong financial results while simultaneously integrating Koch Filter to unlock growth for our Industrial Solutions business segment,” said Steph Disher, Chief Executive Officer of Atmus. “I continue to be inspired by our people’s ability to navigate uncertain markets and execute our four-pillar growth strategy to deliver long-term shareholder value.” First Quarter Results For the first quarter of 2026, Atmus posted net sales of $478 million, compared to $417 million in the first quarter of 2025, an increase of 14.6%. The increase in sales was primarily driven by the acquisition of Koch Filter, the favorable impacts of currency and increases in pricing, partially offset by lower volumes. title: Per-seat CPQ is a tax on growth
summary: Veles is the MCP-native Deal Execution Platform. Manage your entire deal lifecycle with Conversation to Contract optimization built for RevOps and sales leaders.
body_text: Pricing Per-seat CPQ is a tax on growth By Simon Ooley, CEO and Co-Founder of Veles (YC W24) · April 21, 2026 Every CPQ on the market prices the same way. Charge per seat. Add seats when the sales team grows. Bill more every year whether the tool gets used or not. This model is broken. Here is why, and what should replace it. What you are actually paying for Most CPQs list at $75 to $200 per user per month. Multiply by your reps. Add approvers. Add deal desk. Add the admin who keeps the config running. You are spending six figures a year before anyone writes a quote. Then watch how reps actually use it. They do not. They avoid CPQ for as long as possible. They build shadow quotes in spreadsheets, get the deal shaped up, and only drop into the tool at the last possible moment. When they finally are in it, they are stuck for hours clicking through screens to produce a document the customer will spend thirty seconds reading. Most CPQs work this way. Reps hate them, avoid them, and pay the price in hours when they cannot avoid them anymore. That is what your per-seat bill is paying for. The math assumed something that is no longer true. It assumed CPQ was work done by people, at a rate that grew with headcount. More reps meant more quotes. More quotes meant more CPQ usage. Per-seat tracked value because per-seat tracked work. The premise is gone, and the bill keeps coming. The tax has three parts A tax on hiring. Every new rep costs you a seat before they write a single deal. You want to ramp a rep who signs ten deals in their first quarter. You are paying for their CPQ seat for all of it, including the two months they spend reading the playbook. A tax on keeping the seat full. Reps leave. Seats sit assigned. Admins forget to reclaim them. Procurement runs a true-up and you find out you have been paying for forty seats on a team of twenty-eight. The vendor has no incentive to tell you. A tax on being efficient. If your sales org gets better at its job, you are punished. Higher deal volume per rep, same per-seat cost. Your CPQ bill is stuck to your org chart, not to your revenue. None of this gets better once an AI agent joins the team. AI agents killed the seat The per-seat model assumed a human sat in the seat. That assumption is dead. Klarna cut 700 FTE and the licenses that went with them. Customer support platforms are seeing 80 to 90 percent seat compression in teams that adopted AI agents early. Seat-based pricing dropped from 21 percent of SaaS companies to 15 percent in twelve months. Gartner expects 40 percent of enterprise SaaS contracts to include outcome-based components by 2026. IDC thinks 70 percent of vendors will move off pure per-seat by 2028. The market decided. CPQ is the last room to get the memo. The unit is the contract Outcome-based pricing charges for the result, not the chair. Intercom charges $0.99 for every ticket their AI agent resolves. Zendesk charges $1.50 to $2.00 per automated resolution. Salesforce Agentforce charges per agent conversation, not per user. No one is counting humans. For CPQ, the outcome is not ambiguous. A signed contract is the point of the sales motion. Everything a CPQ does is in service of getting there. Configure the product. Price the deal. Build the quote. Route the approvals. Generate the document. Collect the signature. One unit connects all of that. The contract. That is what a CPQ should charge on. Not seats. Not modules. Not “platform access.” A signed contract is the moment value is delivered to both sides of the deal, and it is the only number your CFO, your CRO, and your board actually care about. This flips three things at once. Your CPQ bill tracks your revenue, not your headcount. The vendor only gets paid when you get paid, so a CPQ no one uses stops billing. And a new rep costs you nothing until they close. Your finance team can model it. Your CFO will understand it on the first read. Your reps stop being a line item on a software invoice. Why has no legacy CPQ done this Because seats are easy to bill and hard to lose. Legacy CPQ vendors are locked into the seat model the same way their customers are. Their sales comp runs on seat expansion. Their forecasting runs on seat count. Their enterprise agreements are priced, discounted, and renewed by the seat. Moving a legacy CPQ to outcome-based pricing is not a pricing change. It is a rebuild. Now watch what happens when they try to bolt an agent onto the seat model. If the legacy CPQ stays on per-user pricing and adds an AI agent, they have to charge for the agent too. A seat for the human and a seat for the agent. Your bill goes up while the rep does less work. The vendor cannot resist the seat math, so they double-bill, and the customer ends up paying more for a tool they already hated. The seat model and the agent cannot coexist. The moment a vendor adds an agent, per-seat pricing stops making sense. They either keep billing by the seat and your costs balloon, or they cap the agent at one “AI seat” per user and pretend that reflects the work being done. Neither one holds up at renewal. There is a harder reason underneath all of this. Most legacy CPQs are not confident enough in the outcome to price against it. If the tool only gets the quote 15 percent of the way there and the rep finishes the job in a spreadsheet, the vendor cannot charge for the contract. They can only charge for access to the tool and hope no one notices the gap. An outcome price requires a product that actually produces the outcome. What we are doing at Veles We built Veles so the agent builds the quote and the rep reviews. The unit of value is a signed contract, not a seat. So that is how we want to charge. Every team starts on a free tier. Run up to 25 contracts before you pay us a dollar. After that, pricing tracks the work. Contracts executed, not seats assigned. Ramp a new rep at no license cost. Hit a slow quarter and the bill drops with it. Hire ten more reps and your CPQ bill only moves when deals move. That is what pricing should do. Track the contract, not the chair. If you are running CPQ today and watching your per-seat bill grow faster than your revenue, the problem is not your config. The problem is the pricing model. That is the part no rep will ever fix, no matter how many seats you buy. Simon, Veles ’ CEO

title: How to register as self-employed in the UK and US
summary: Learn how to register as self-employed in the UK and US. Step-by-step process, deadlines, and what to do after registration. Start your freelance career today.
body_text: Starting your own business is an exciting step, but before you start earning, it's important to understand the legal and tax requirements that come with being self-employed. Proper registration ensures your business, whether freelance, consulting, product-based, or professional services, remains compliant, avoids penalties, and is built on a solid foundation. While the process is relatively straightforward, the rules differ significantly between the UK and the US. To register as self-employed in the UK, sign up for Self Assessment on the HMRC website. You must register by 5 October following the tax year you started trading. In the US, no formal "self-employed registration" exists. You file taxes as a sole proprietor using Schedule C with your annual tax return. Most states require a business licence or sales tax permit. This guide explains how self-employment registration works in both countries, the documents you'll need and the key deadlines to keep in mind before you start trading. What does it mean to be self-employed? Being self-employed means you work for yourself rather than an employer. Instead of earning a salary through payroll, you generate income by providing services, selling products or running your own business. The terms below are often used interchangeably, but they have different meanings: Self-employed: A broad term for anyone who works for themselves instead of an employer. Freelancer: A self-employed person who usually works with multiple clients on short or long-term contracts. Sole proprietor (US): The default business structure for self-employed individuals, where the owner and business are legally the same entity. Limited company (UK): A separate legal entity from its owner, offering greater liability protection but with additional reporting and compliance requirements. Also read: Freelancer vs Employee Tax: What You Owe Compared How to register as self-employed in the UK If you're starting a business, freelancing or earning income outside traditional employment, you'll need to register with HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) as self-employed. The process is straightforward, but it's important to register on time to avoid penalties and ensure you're meeting your tax obligations. Create a Government Gateway account on the HMRC website if you don't already have one. Register for Self Assessment using your Government Gateway credentials. This tells HMRC that you'll be responsible for reporting and paying your own taxes. Receive your Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR) number. HMRC will send this to you after your registration is processed. You'll need it whenever you file tax returns or communicate with HMRC. Choose your business structure. Most people start as sole traders, while others may prefer a limited company for liability protection and potential tax advantages. Also read: Freelancing vs Full-Time employment: When should you switch? How to register as self-employed in the US Starting as a self-employed professional in the US is straightforward once you understand the process. The IRS receives approximately 27 to 30 million nonfarm sole proprietorship returns each year , highlighting just how common self-employment has become. Here's how to get started: Choose a business structure: Most freelancers begin as a sole proprietorship, while others may prefer an LLC for liability protection or an S Corporation for potential tax advantages. Apply for an Employer Identification Number (EIN): Sole proprietors can often use their Social Security Number, but an EIN is recommended if you hire employees, open a business bank account or operate as an LLC. Register with your state if required: Depending on your location and business activity, you may need a business licence, sales tax permit or local operating permit. File your taxes correctly: Self-employed sole proprietors report business income and expenses using Schedule C, submitted alongside Form 1040 during the annual tax filing process. Keep accurate financial records throughout the year to simplify reporting and maximise eligible deductions. What you'll need before registering as self-employed Preparing the right information before you register will make the process quicker and help you avoid delays. While the exact requirements differ between the UK and the US, most self-employed individuals should have the following details ready: National Insurance Number (UK) or Social Security Number (US) for tax identification. Business name , if you've chosen to trade under one instead of your personal name. Business address , which may be your home address or your registered business location. Business start date , showing when you began or plan to begin trading. Business activity , including a clear description of the products you sell or the services you provide. Estimated annual income , which may be required for tax registration, licensing or planning your tax obligations. Contact details , including your phone number and email address for official correspondence. Business bank account details , if you've already opened one to keep your personal and business finances separate. Having this information ready before you begin can save time and make your registration process much smoother, whether you're registering in the UK or the US. What to do after registering as self-employed Registering your business is only the first step. Once you're officially self-employed, it's important to build good financial habits from the beginning. Open a separate business bank account to keep your personal and business finances apart, making it easier to track cash flow, manage expenses and prepare accurate financial records throughout the year. Next, create a system for recording every payment you receive and every business expense you incur. If you're based in the US, set aside money for quarterly estimated tax payments to avoid penalties. In the UK, regularly save a portion of your income so you're prepared for your annual Self Assessment tax bill and National Insurance contributions. If you work with international clients, managing foreign payments is just as important. Grey gives freelancers foreign currency accounts in USD, GBP and EUR, allowing you to receive payments like a local, hold multiple currencies and convert your earnings at competitive exchange rates before transferring funds to your local bank account. Common mistakes to avoid when registering as self-employed Missing registration deadlines: Delaying your registration can lead to penalties, unnecessary stress and compliance issues. Make sure you understand the deadlines that apply in your country and complete your registration as soon as you start trading. Mixing personal and business finances: Using one bank account for everything makes it harder to track income, claim legitimate business expenses and prepare accurate tax returns. A separate business account keeps your finances organised from day one. Failing to keep receipts and financial records: Keep receipts, invoices and bank statements for every business transaction. Good record-keeping simplifies tax filing, supports expense claims and protects you if your tax authority requests additional information. Choosing the wrong business structure: Selecting a sole proprietorship, limited company or LLC without understanding the tax and legal implications could cost you money. Review your options carefully as your income and business grow. Ignoring your tax obligations: Don't wait until tax season to think about your finances. Set money aside regularly for taxes and understand whether you need to make estimated payments or file annual returns. Not planning for international payments: If you work with overseas clients, relying only on traditional bank transfers can increase costs. Consider payment solutions that make receiving foreign currency faster, more affordable and easier to manage. Frequently asked questions When do I need to register as self-employed? The timing depends on where you live. In the UK, you must register for Self Assessment by 5 October following the end of the tax year in which you started trading. In the US, there is no formal self-employment registration, but you must meet federal, state and local tax and licensing requirements before or shortly after starting your business. Can I be employed and self-employed at the same time? Yes. Many people have a full-time or part-time job while running a freelance business on the side. You'll continue paying tax through your employer, but you'll also need to declare your self-employed income separately and meet any additional tax obligations that apply to your freelance earnings. Do I need a business name to register as self-employed? No. You can trade using your own legal name if you prefer. However, many freelancers choose a business name to create a stronger brand and appear more professional. If you do, make sure the name complies with your country's business registration rules and doesn't infringe existing trademarks. What is a UTR number? A Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR) is a 10-digit number issued by HMRC to individuals and businesses in the UK. It's used to identify you for tax purposes and is required when filing your Self Assessment tax return, communicating with HMRC or managing your online tax account. What's the difference between a UTR and an EIN? A UTR is a UK tax reference issued by HMRC to identify taxpayers for Self Assessment. An Employer Identification Number (EIN) is issued by the IRS in the US and identifies businesses for federal tax purposes. They serve similar administrative functions but belong to different tax systems. Can I receive payments from international clients into my Grey account? Yes. title: Debit Note and Credit Note: Meaning, Key Differences and Examples
summary: Confused about debit notes and credit notes? Understand their meaning, key differences, GST treatment, accounting entries, examples, and business use cases.
body_text: Table of Contents Toggle TL;DR: A debit note is usually issued by the buyer to request an invoice adjustment for damaged goods, short supply, pricing errors, or overcharges. A credit note is generally issued by the seller to confirm the adjustment. Together, they help businesses maintain accurate accounting records, simplify GST compliance, and streamline invoice reconciliation. Businesses often need to correct invoices because of damaged goods, pricing errors, short deliveries, or product returns. Instead of cancelling the original invoice, companies use debit notes and credit notes to record these adjustments while keeping their accounting records accurate. Although these documents are commonly used in business transactions, many people confuse their purpose and when each should be issued. Understanding the difference is especially important for businesses in India, where debit notes and credit notes also play a key role in GST compliance and invoice reconciliation. What is a Debit Note? A debit note is a business document issued by the buyer (purchaser) to inform the seller that the invoice amount should be adjusted due to an issue with the supplied goods or services. It acts as a formal request asking the seller to reduce the payable amount or review the invoice because something doesn’t match the original agreement. A debit note is commonly issued when: Goods are damaged during delivery Fewer products are delivered than ordered The seller charges more than the agreed price Incorrect products are supplied Additional charges are applied by mistake Instead of immediately requesting a refund, the buyer first sends a debit note explaining the issue. The seller then reviews the claim and, if accepted, issues a credit note to complete the adjustment. Information Included in a Debit Note A debit note typically contains: Debit note number Date of issue Buyer and seller details Original invoice number Description of the issue Quantity affected Amount to be adjusted GST details (if applicable) Authorized signature Example of a Debit Note Imagine a retailer purchases 50 laptops from a supplier for ₹500,000. After delivery, the retailer discovers that five laptops are damaged. Instead of paying the full invoice amount, the retailer issues a debit note requesting an adjustment for the damaged units. The supplier then verifies the claim before issuing a credit note. Also read: What is Goods Received Note (GRN)? What is a Credit Note? A credit note is a document issued by the seller (vendor) to reduce the amount payable by the buyer after accepting a claim related to damaged goods, sales returns, invoice corrections, pricing mistakes, or billing errors. Think of it as the seller’s confirmation that the invoice has been corrected. Rather than issuing a completely new invoice, businesses use credit notes to maintain a proper audit trail while updating the customer’s outstanding balance. Common reasons for issuing a credit note include: Customer returns goods Invoice amount was higher than agreed Wrong GST amount was charged Pricing errors Discounts offered after invoicing Seller accepts a buyer’s debit note Once the credit note is issued, the buyer’s outstanding amount is reduced accordingly. Information Included in a Credit Note A standard credit note generally includes: Credit note number Date Seller and buyer details Original invoice number Reason for issuing the credit note Amount credited Applicable GST adjustment Signature or authorization Example of a Credit Note Continuing the previous example, after inspecting the returned goods, the supplier confirms that five laptops were damaged during transportation. The supplier issues a credit note for the value of those laptops, reducing the buyer’s payable amount and updating both parties’ accounting records. Debit Note and Credit Note: What’s the Difference? The main difference between a debit note and a credit note lies in who issues the document and why it is issued. A debit note is generally raised by the buyer to notify the seller about an issue with an invoice or delivered goods and request an adjustment . A credit note, on the other hand, is issued by the seller after accepting the buyer’s claim to confirm that the invoice has been corrected. Although these documents serve different purposes, they often work together. In many business transactions, a debit note initiates the correction process, while the credit note finalizes it. Debit Note vs Credit Note Comparison Basis Debit Note Credit Note Issued By Buyer (Purchaser) Seller (Vendor) Purpose Requests an adjustment to the invoice Confirms the adjustment and reduces the invoice amount Raised When Goods are damaged, short supplied, incorrectly priced, or overcharged Seller accepts the buyer’s claim, goods are returned, or invoice corrections are required Impact on Buyer Requests a reduction in the payable amount Reduces the buyer’s outstanding balance Impact on Seller Indicates a claim has been raised Acknowledges and accepts the claim Relation to Invoice References the original invoice to request correction References the original invoice to confirm correction GST Usage Used to initiate GST-related invoice adjustments Used to complete GST adjustments after acceptance Accounting Effect Purchase-related adjustment Sales-related adjustment Business Purpose Notify the seller of discrepancies Officially record the approved adjustment Typical Sequence Issued first Usually issued after the debit note is accepted How Debit Notes and Credit Notes Work Together These documents are not competitors – they are complementary. Which Document Should You Use? Situation Debit Note Credit Note Goods damaged Buyer issues Seller issues after approval Short supply Buyer issues Seller confirms adjustment Invoice overcharged Buyer issues Seller corrects invoice Sales return Buyer requests adjustment Seller issues credit note Discount after invoicing — Seller issues credit note Debit Note and Credit Note in India Debit notes and credit notes are widely used by Indian businesses to correct invoices without cancelling the original transaction. They help businesses maintain accurate accounting records, resolve billing disputes , process sales returns, and comply with GST requirements . These documents are commonly used across industries such as manufacturing, wholesale, retail, eCommerce, logistics, and B2B services, where invoice adjustments are a regular part of business operations. Some of the most common situations include: Sales returns Damaged or defective goods Short deliveries Incorrect pricing Excess or duplicate billing Discounts offered after invoicing GST adjustments By properly issuing debit notes and credit notes, businesses create a clear audit trail that simplifies reconciliation and reduces accounting errors. GST Perspective: Why Debit Notes and Credit Notes Matter Under India’s GST system, debit notes and credit notes play an important role in recording invoice adjustments while maintaining transparency in tax reporting. These documents help businesses: Correct taxable value after an invoice has been issued Record sales returns Adjust GST payable or receivable Maintain accurate books of accounts Simplify GST reconciliation during return filing Instead of cancelling and reissuing invoices, businesses can use debit notes and credit notes to document legitimate changes while preserving the original transaction history. Note: Businesses should ensure that every debit note or credit note clearly references the original invoice and complies with applicable GST documentation requirements. Accounting Entries for Debit Notes and Credit Notes The accounting treatment depends on whether you are recording the transaction from the buyer’s or seller’s perspective. Debit Note Entry (Buyer’s Books) When goods are returned or the invoice value is reduced: Supplier A/c Dr. To Purchase Return A/c This entry records the reduction in the amount payable to the supplier. Credit Note Entry (Seller’s Books) When the seller accepts the claim: Sales Return A/c Dr. To Customer A/c This entry reduces the customer’s outstanding balance and records the sales adjustment. Note: The exact accounting treatment may vary depending on the organization’s accounting policies and ERP system. Debit Note Format Although formats vary across businesses and accounting software, a standard debit note generally includes the following information. Field Description Debit Note Number Unique reference number Date Date of issue Buyer Details Name, address, GSTIN (if applicable) Seller Details Name, address, GSTIN Original Invoice Number Invoice being corrected Reason Damage, short supply, pricing error, etc. Product Details Item description and quantity Adjustment Amount Amount to be reduced GST Details Applicable GST adjustment Authorized Signature Buyer authorization Credit Note Format A standard credit note generally contains: Field Description Credit Note Number Unique reference number Date Date of issue Seller Details Name, address, GSTIN Buyer Details Name, address, GSTIN Original Invoice Number Reference invoice Reason Sales return, overcharge, pricing correction Amount Credited Value being adjusted GST Adjustment Applicable tax details Authorized Signature Seller authorization Common Mistakes to Avoid Even though debit notes and credit notes are straightforward documents, mistakes can create accounting discrepancies, GST reconciliation issues, or audit challenges. Here are some common errors businesses should avoid: Mistake Why It Matters Not referencing the original invoice Makes reconciliation difficult Issuing the wrong document Can lead to incorrect accounting entries Missing GST details May create compliance issues Incorrect adjustment amount Results in inaccurate financial records Poor document numbering Makes audit tracking difficult Delayed issuance Can complicate month-end closing and reconciliation Following a standardized process for issuing debit notes and credit notes helps maintain accurate records and reduces the risk of disputes. Best Practices for Businesses To improve accounting accuracy and maintain proper documentation, businesses should follow these best practices: Always reference the original invoice number. Clearly state the reason for the adjustment. Include supporting documents where applicable (such as delivery reports or return requests). Ensure GST details are correctly captured. Issue the document as soon as the discrepancy is identified or approved. Keep debit notes and credit notes securely stored for future reference and audits. Regularly reconcile adjustments with accounting records and GST returns . Implementing these practices can help businesses streamline invoice management and reduce reconciliation errors. Real-World Example Scenario: ABC Traders purchases 100 office chairs from XYZ Furniture for ₹500,000 . Upon delivery, 10 chairs are found to be damaged. Step 1: ABC Traders issues a debit note requesting an adjustment for the damaged chairs. Step 2: XYZ Furniture verifies the claim and issues a credit note for the approved amount. Result: The invoice is adjusted, the buyer pays only for the undamaged goods, and both parties update their accounting records and GST documentation. Conclusion Debit notes and credit notes are essential documents for correcting invoice-related issues without cancelling the original transaction. A debit note is generally issued by the buyer to report discrepancies, while a credit note is issued by the seller to confirm and record the approved adjustment. Using these documents correctly helps businesses maintain accurate financial records, simplify GST compliance, and ensure smooth reconciliation between buyers and sellers.
